Just now

--

I want to tell you about the day I made Claude Code worse at its job by trying to make it better.
I’d been using it for a few weeks on a side project, and every session started the same way: reminding it which package manager to use, telling it to run the tests, asking it to stop touching files I hadn’t mentioned. So I did the obvious thing. I opened my CLAUDE.md file and I started writing. Rules for everything. Style preferences, naming conventions, a little essay about the architecture, a list of every command I could think of. By the end it was maybe 250 lines and I felt like a responsible adult.
The next morning Claude ignored half of it.
Not in a dramatic way. It just quietly went back to old habits — wrong package manager, skipped tests, the works. And the thing I couldn’t figure out at the time is that the file wasn’t broken. It was too big. I’d walked straight into the single most common mistake people make with this file, and it took me a while and a lot of reading to understand why.
So let me save you that detour. Here’s how CLAUDE.md actually works, what to put in it, what to leave out, and how the whole picture shifted in early 2026 when Claude Code started writing its own memory.
